title: Oxygen Partial Pressure Effect on Atomic Nickel Migration in NixCeO2-x Aerogel under Electron Irradiation
content: Hydrogen gas production, predominantly performed at petroleum refineries, is a growing global industry. The current industrial standard for H2 production is steam methane reforming. Additional H2 production from the CO biproduct is achieved by the water-gas shift (WGS) reaction, converting H2O and CO into CO2 and H2 using Fe-Cr catalysts [1, 2]. However, Fe-Cr catalysts are inefficient and leach toxic, water-soluble Cr6+ resulting in high disposal costs and environmental degradation [2, 3]. To address these limitations, identifying and characterizing alternate catalysts for WGS reaction with improved efficiency, selectivity, and reduced toxicity has driven a wide array of research over the past 30 years. Specifically, a reliable sol-gel synthesis produces CeO2 aerogels with atomically dispersed Ni loadings between 0 and 20 atomic percent (at%) with the 5 at% Ni aerogel yielding 97% CO conversion efficiency while maintaining low (0.09%) CH4 production [4]. The mechanism by which atomic Ni within the CeO2 aerogel architecture affects the catalytic reaction remains unanswered. The impact of high porosity of the covalently bonded CeO2 aerogel domains, Ni mobility in a catalytic environment, and Ni location withing a given aerogel domain remain unanswered.
